claims.citation: New York Herald, 12 August 1866, p. 3, col. 4
claims.verbatim: QUEBEC, Aug 6—Arr brig Cuba, Holmes, Antwerp.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 3 July 1866, p. 5, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The Cuba, 24th of June, reports:—Nothing positive
had transpired as to the Ministerial crisis.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 6 July 1866, p. 4, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
Our special correspondence from Vienna, Berlin and
Paris[?], dated to the latest moment previous to the depar-
ture[?] of the Cuba from Queenstown (June 23), is published
in[?] the HERALD to-day, with a compilation from the latest
European[?] files.

claims.claim: Brought news from Vienna, Paris, and Berlin, to 1866-06-23
claims.citation: New York Herald, 6 July 1866, p. 8, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
Our special correspondence from Vienna, Paris, and
Berlin, dated to the latest moment prior to the sailing of
the Cuba (June 23) from Queenstown, with the compila-
tion from our foreign files, which we publish this morn-
ing,

claims.citation: New York Herald, 3 July 1866, p. 9, col. 1
claims.verbatim: The Cuba's news, up to the 29th ult., quickly followed, and the price further gave way to 153 1/8[?].

The steamship Cuba, from Liverpool on the
23d, via Queenstown on the 24th ult., with
dates three days later, has arrived at New
York.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 3 July 1866, p. 6, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
By the arrival yesterday of the steamships Bremen,
Bavaria, City of Boston and Merrimac, at this port, and
Cuba, at Halifax, we received news from Europe, by
mail and telegraph, to the 24th of June, seven days later.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 5 July 1866, p. 8, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The European mails by the Cuba reached this city
from Boston last night. Our files are dated to the 23d
of June.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 3 July 1866, p. 5, col. 6
claims.verbatim:
Sailing of the Cuba.
HALIFAX, July 2, 1866.
The Cuba sailed at six P. M. for Boston, where she will
be due early Wednesday morning.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 10 July 1866, p. 5, col. 2
claims.verbatim:
By the steamer Cuba, Captain Rollins, which arrived
at Baltimore on the 8th inst., we have received important
news from Havana to the 4th inst.

claims.citation: The Sun (New York), 10 July 1866, p. 1, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
BALTIMORE, JULY 9.—The SUN publishes the fol-
lowing account of a rumored revolt in Cuba, which
it received specially from Captain Rollins, of the
steamer Cuba, which arrived yesterday from Havana
on the 4th instant:
